content.text:
Finding submitted.

**LICENSE — deviation (fallback redline at p0346).**

- **Investigation:** No affirmative licence grant exists anywhere in the Transfer and Servicing Agreement. Searches for "license", "grant", "right to use", "software", "irrevocable" and "intellectual property" returned only (i) regulatory qualification licences (p0234, p0259, p0272), (ii) security-interest "Grants" (defined at p0763 as a pledge/lien, not an IP licence), and (iii) the transition provision at p0346.
- **Direction check:** The power of attorney at p0105 runs *from* the Issuer *to* the Servicer and is expressly revocable by us — a benefit to our side, so not flagged.
- **The problem:** p0346 is an express refusal to license the Servicer's processes, models and servicing software to any Successor Servicer or third party. That leaves our Affiliates excluded with no path to add them and nothing transferable to a successor — both fallback elements fail, and it sits in walk-away territory.
- **Cure:** One surgical replace converting the disclaimer sentence into a licence to the Issuer, extending to Issuer Affiliates on written notice and transferable to an M&A successor, with the confidentiality / legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection carve-out preserved verbatim so no contradictory mechanic survives. Preferred perpetual/irrevocable, subscription-termination and contractor elements were not added — this structure has no paid-up or subscription licence construct, and the checklist is the ceiling.
